name: Britannia Industries Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest listed biscuit maker (Good Day, Tiger, NutriChoice, Milk Bikis, Marie Gold) with bread, cakes, rusk and dairy (cheese, beverages, yoghurt) adjacencies. TTM sales Rs 19,529 cr, EBITDA Rs 3,600 cr (18.4% margin), net profit Rs 2,610 cr; ROCE 56%, near-zero net leverage. Domestic business is the bulk; international (UAE/Middle East, Africa) is mid-single-digit % of sales (model knowledge). Promoters 50.55% (Wadia group, held via Bombay Burmah and others); FIIs have fallen from 15.6% to 12.9% in two quarters while DIIs (incl. LIC at >5%) rose to 21.4%. Stock is at/near a 52-week low (Rs 4,983, -15% 12m) on volume softness, input-cost inflation and a margin miss in Q1 FY27.

exposures.mechanism: Flour/maida ~15% of Rs 15,929 cr cost base = Rs 2,389 cr; wheat +10% -> +Rs 239 cr = 6.6% of Rs 3,600 cr EBITDA. ~40% passed through via price/grammage within 2-3 qtrs => 4.0% unrecovered; EV/MCap 1.0; persistence 0.4 => -1.6. Empirical sensitivity is +1.29 (t=+2.2), wrong-signed vs mechanism (wheat rallies coincide with defensive rotation / inflation hedging); shrunk to -1.2 with range crossing zero. Wheat is -14.7% in 1m per factor_state, a near-term tailwind.

exposures.mechanism: Palm oil/vegetable fat ~9% of costs (Rs 1,434 cr); +10% -> Rs 143 cr = 4.0% of EBITDA; 60% unrecovered x persistence 0.4 x EV/MCap 1.0 => -0.95. Series proxy is soybean oil (ZS=F) so basis risk vs palm. Palm/crude inflation flagged in Oct-2026 FMCG Q2 margin-squeeze coverage (Economic Times 2026-10-11).

Overlaps F_PACKAGING (avoid full stacking); empirical -- not significant in pack. Brent is +15% in 3m and +50% in 12m (factor_state), so the cumulative headwind is real.

exposures.mechanism: Urban ~60% of domestic sales; +5pp urban consumption growth ~ +2.5pp revenue growth (volume elasticity ~0.8) x ~45% gross-margin drop-through = Rs 220 cr = 6.1% of EBITDA; EV/MCap 1.0; persistence 0.5 => +3.0, haircut to 2.5 for pricing/mix drag. TTM sales growth is only 7% vs 5y CAGR 7.8%.

exposures.mechanism: Rural ~40% of sales; +5pp rural growth ~ +1.5pp revenue x 45% drop-through = Rs 132 cr = 3.7% of EBITDA x persistence 0.5 => +1.8. Low-unit-price packs (Rs 5-10) are the most rural-sensitive.

supply_chain.note: ITC is the main organised competitor in biscuits; Parle leads in glucose/Rs5 packs.
